title: elymus acutus subsp. obtusiusculus
intro: Elymus acutus subsp. obtusiusculus, commonly known as blue wildrye, is a type of grass native to North America, belonging to the family Poaceae. This plant is valued for its medicinal properties, which include anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antioxidant effects that promote wound healing, reduce fever, and alleviate digestive issues. The bioactive constituents of blue wildrye include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and sesquiterpenes, which contribute to its therapeutic actions such as antimicrobial, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory properties. Traditional uses of blue wildrye include treating respiratory problems, skin conditions, and gastrointestinal disorders, highlighting its potential as a natural remedy for various health concerns.
